status: source-only transactional APC/MX recovery and RPM response correlation; no native qualification
APC_contract: A failed VCTL command can have changed hardware. Reset and resubmit the old physical selector directly through SAW before returning the original error.
Require matching selector plus idle PMIC state, apply conservative slew delay, and verify PMIC range/selector.
Recovery forces PWM for a possible voltage rise, retries once, and stops the kernel if the old rail cannot be confirmed after two attempts.
A failed AUTO-mode restore after confirmed voltage remains a deferred mode error with the voltage held in PWM.
RPM_contract: Allocate per-channel nonzero IDs under the send mutex.
Reinitialize completion and publish the pending ID under an IRQ-safe spinlock before send.
Bounds-check unaligned response TLVs and require exactly one matching request ID before completing.
Complete while holding the response lock; retire the pending request on all send/wait outcomes so late or duplicate replies cannot satisfy a later request.
MX_contract: A failed active MX vote may already have applied, including after a timeout.
Force the prior regulator consumer request through regulator_sync_voltage, whose RPM set_voltage path sends a fresh request.
Retry restoration once and stop the kernel if the prior vote cannot be confirmed. This depends on request-correlated RPM acknowledgements.
A failed MX reduction can remain a deferred error only after the old floor is restored; subsequent APC increases may rely on that restored floor.
CPR_contract: Restore feedback for the confirmed old corner after a failed performance request. Keep feedback off after an initial failed nominal request or system suspend; do not leave a previously adapted high-frequency point permanently without feedback merely because genpd cached its old state.

actual_caller_chain.functions: unmodified OPP _set_opp/_set_required_opps/_set_opp_level and genpd callbacks, actual CPR performance callback and coupled helper, actual SAW transaction helper; regulator request caching and I/O are modeled

APC_fault_cases.fail_stop_mechanism: kernel panic mocked with longjmp; no host or device kernel stopped

verification.MX_fault_cases: actual kernel regulator_sync_voltage and RPM regulator callbacks; before/after-effect failures, forced old-vote restoration, retry, future APC rise and persistent-failure no-return controls

interleavings: timed-out request followed by late old ACK
old ACK while a newer request waits

verification.build_scope: Clang ARM objects only; no full kernel, package, new boot image or installation

full_series_reproduction.result: all changed files reproduced byte for byte

verification.checkpatch: all four patches have 0 errors and 0 warnings; SAW has one atomic-context udelay suggestion, MX has one existing uV naming suggestion; RPM and feedback patches have no checks

hardware_limits: Models test transaction ordering, not physical voltage/settling, SAW reset semantics or real RPM firmware behavior.
Native RAM qualification, CPUfreq attachment/bin filtering, complete current DMP/display source reconstruction, packaging, rollback and broader hardware acceptance remain open.
Deeper suspend remains unsupported by the source candidate until RPM sleep-vote handoff is implemented.

installed_baseline.scope: read-only baseline check; no device changes or native fault injection
